CVSF Process Simulator

User manual · simulation, Bayesian calibration with the experiment database, and Bayesian experimental design
Model code CVSF_Model_Filtration_Deliquoring_Washing_V01 · M.P. Meier, M. Vogel, L. Ohm · TU Dortmund University

The CVSF Process Simulator is the graphical interface of the mechanistic model of the continuous vacuum screw filter (CVSF): cake filtration, gas deliquoring, and evaporation in the filtration module as well as two-stage displacement washing. Besides predictive simulation, it collects experimental data of completed CVSF runs, improves the model parameters continuously by Bayesian calibration, and plans the experiments that improve the model most.

1 · Overview: three modes and the improvement loop

ModeQuestionResult
SimulationHow does the CVSF behave for given particles, operating point, and apparatus? end of cake formation z_S1, residual moisture along the apparatus and at the outlet, residence time, filling degree, filter cake properties, design maps, wash curves
CalibrationHow do new experimental data change the model parameters? experiment database with activation checkboxes, Bayesian recalibration, versioned model states
Experiment designWhich experiment improves the model most? ranked plan of the next experiments, maps of the information gain, plan as Excel template

The three modes form a loop (Figure 1): the current model state is used for simulation and for planning experiments; the measured data are added to the experiment database, the model is recalibrated with all active data, and the checked new model state becomes the current model for simulation and the next planning round.

2 · Installation and start

Requirements

Python ≥ 3.11 (e.g. Miniforge) with the packages of requirements.txt (numpy, scipy, pandas, openpyxl, matplotlib, SALib, streamlit, plotly). Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome for the application window.

Desktop application (recommended, Windows)

  1. Copy the package folder CVSF_Model_Filtration_Deliquoring_Washing_V01 to a permanent location.
  2. Double-click install_desktop_app.bat (or, in the Miniforge Prompt with the desired environment activated: python install_desktop_app.py). Missing packages are installed, and the shortcut CVSF Process Simulator with the CVSF icon is created on the desktop and in the start menu.
  3. Double-click the desktop icon: the model runs in the background (no console window), and the interface opens in its own application window (Figure 2). Closing the window stops the model.

Alternatives: start_gui.bat / start_gui.sh or streamlit run gui/app.py (opens in the web browser). Everything runs locally; no data leave the computer. After moving the package folder, run the installation again; python install_desktop_app.py --remove removes the shortcuts.

Storage folder

The experiment database, the change log, and the parameter sets / model states are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CVSF_Process_Simulator. The folder can be changed in the mode Calibration (tab Experiment database) – e.g. to a shared network folder, so that the whole working group uses the same data and model states.

3 · Mode Simulation

The sidebar (Figure 3) contains, from top to bottom:

  • Mode switch (Simulation, Calibration, Experiment design).
  • Model parameter set: ★ marks the current model state of the material system (after the first adopted recalibration; before, the reference set of the filtration study). Other sets can be selected for comparison.
  • Particle system: particle shape; PSD as Excel file of the dynamic image analysis (example data, upload, or path), as log-normal distribution (d50,3, σg), or from the characteristic diameters d10,3/d50,3/d90,3; sphericity.
  • Operating point: Q_susp, w_solid, n_screw (or target filling degree), Δp, ϑ_susp.
  • Apparatus and screw design: current or previous module generation, screws (a)–(c) or custom.
  • Air flow through the module (evaporation) and model parameters (advanced).
  • Run simulation. Input sets can be saved and loaded as JSON.

The key figures (Figure 4, top) summarize the result: end of cake formation z_S1 compared with the filter length, residual moisture at the outlet with its 95 % interval from the uncertainty of B, θm and residence times, filling degree, porosity and cake resistance, and the minimum Δp for complete cake formation on the filter medium.

Axial profiles are model predictions: the enclosed module does not allow spatially resolved sampling; experimentally, the residual moisture is accessible only at the module outlet.

Further tabs

Tab Export provides the results (JSON), the residual moisture profile (CSV), and the inputs (JSON); tab Model & references summarizes the model structure, validity ranges, and references.

4 · Mode Calibration (experiment database and Bayesian recalibration)

The detailed, screenshot-based guide for the Excel template is docs/Guide_Experimental_Data_Template.pdf (also downloadable in the interface). In short:

  1. Add data: download the Excel template, fill in the material system and one row per experiment (RTD → θm; filter cake test → ε, α_FC; CVSF run → residual moisture at the outlet with PSD and operating point), upload it together with the PSD files, check the status of every row (usable for, missing information, plausibility/units), and add the data as a dataset with name, operator, date, and description.
  2. Experiment database: each dataset and each experiment has an active checkbox; deactivation requires a reason and is logged (figure below). Deactivated data stay stored and can be reactivated at any time.
  3. Recalibrate model: Bayesian recalibration with all active experiments of the material system, starting again from the reference parameter set of the filtration study – deactivated data therefore have no influence on the new model state (figure below).
  4. Adopt the checked result as the current model state ★; earlier model states remain available.
StageParametersExperimental data
1μs, a, b (θm correlation, Fit 1)θm from RTD measurements; screw, n_screw
2A (sphericity correction, Fit F1)filter cake porosity and/or specific cake resistance; PSD
3B (equilibrium saturation factor, Fit F2)residual moisture at the outlet; PSD; operating point

5 · Mode Experiment design (Bayesian experimental design)

The mode answers the question which experiments would make the model better and more accurate? It uses the current knowledge of the model – the selected model state, i.e. the posterior of the latest Bayesian calibration with all active experiments – and evaluates candidate experiments by the information they are expected to provide about the model parameters.

5.1 Procedure

  1. Choose the current knowledge: model state ★ (default) or another parameter set.
  2. Choose the experiment types and their relative effort (cost): RTD measurement (informs μs, a, b), filter cake test (informs A), CVSF run with residual moisture measurement (informs B). The cost weights trade off information against effort, e.g. a CVSF run with 2 against a filter cake test with 0.5.
  3. Define the design spaces (figure below): range of n_screw for the RTD measurements; particle shape, σg, d50,3 range, and agglomeration degree range for the filter cake tests; for the CVSF runs two operating parameters as axes (from Q_susp, n_screw, Δp, ϑ_susp, w_solid) with ranges, the grid resolution, and the fixed conditions (particle system, setup, screw, remaining operating parameters).
  4. Set the number of planned experiments k and the exploration weight w.
  5. Compute experiment plan. RTD and filter cake candidates take less than 2 s; each grid point of the CVSF runs requires two evaluations of the filtration module (approx. 0.6 s per point, parallelized).
  6. Evaluate the result (section 5.3) and download the plan as Excel template: the settings of the planned experiments are filled in, the measured columns are empty.
  7. Carry out the experiments, fill in the measured values (and PSD files), and upload the file in the mode Calibration; recalibrate and adopt the new model state. The next planning round then starts from the improved knowledge.

5.2 Method

  • Current knowledge: parameter vector p = (μs, a, b, A, B) with mean and covariance Σ of the model state.
  • Linearization: for each candidate experiment x the model calculates the measured quantities y(x) and their sensitivities J = ∂y/∂p at the current parameters. R is the measurement/model uncertainty of the measured quantities (same values as in the calibration).
  • Expected information gain (D-optimal Bayesian design, in nat):

EIG(x) = ½ · ln det( I + R⁻¹ J Σ Jᵀ )     Σ′ = Σ − Σ Jᵀ (J Σ Jᵀ + R)⁻¹ J Σ

  • Sequential batch Bayesian optimization: the plan is built step by step; in each step the candidate with the largest acquisition value

a(x) = EIG(x | Σk) / cost (normalized) + w · novelty(x)

  • is selected; then Σ is updated with Σ′ (as if the experiment had been carried out), so that the next selection accounts for the information already planned. The novelty term (distance to existing and planned experiments in the normalized design space) adds exploration: experiments in regions without data also test the model structure, which the parameter information alone does not capture. w = 0 gives pure information gain; larger w favors new regions.
  • Existing experiments are the data of the filtration study (13 RTD values, 8 filter cakes, 12 residual moistures) and all active experiments of the material system in the experiment database.

5.3 Results and their interpretation

ElementMeaning
key figures per parameterexpected reduction of the standard deviation of μs, a, b, A, B after all planned experiments (green: ≥ 10 %)
rank, type, experimentorder of the plan and settings of each experiment
measurequantities to be measured (θm; ε, α_FC, PSD; residual moisture at the outlet, PSD)
EIG_natinformation gain of the experiment given the experiments planned before it
novelty0 = close to existing data, 1 = far from existing data
SD↓ … (cum.)expected cumulative reduction of the parameter standard deviation up to this rank
Example – current reference model state (5 experiments, w = 0.3, cost RTD 1 / cake 0.5 / CVSF run 2): the plan consists of three filter cake tests with strongly agglomerated particle systems (Ag3 ≈ 0.75 at different d50,3) and RTD measurements at n_screw = 5 rpm with the screws (b) and (c). Expected reduction of the parameter uncertainties: A ≈ −39 %, a ≈ −32 %, b ≈ −14 %, μs ≈ −5 %, B ≈ 0 %.
Why are CVSF runs hardly selected? The residual moisture scatters by approx. 3.6 %-pts. around the model (measurement and model deviation of the filtration study). One additional value therefore reduces the uncertainty of B only slightly; replicates, different particle systems, and operating points close to the deliquoring equilibrium are more effective. The map of the CVSF runs nevertheless shows the most informative operating points.
Limits. The EIG refers to the parameters of the existing model structure and is based on a local linearization at the current parameters. Systematic model deviations (e.g. a missing physical effect) are not captured by the information gain; they are addressed by the exploration term and by checking the new data in the calibration (parity plots, leave-one-out Q²). Candidates outside the validated ranges (e.g. n_screw > 5 rpm, other material systems) are extrapolations of the model. The washing model is not part of the experiment design in this version.

6 · Recommended procedure for continuous model improvement

  1. Plan (mode Experiment design): select the current model state ★, the experiment types and costs, and the design spaces that are technically feasible; compute the plan; check that the recommended settings can be realized; download the plan.
  2. Experiment: carry out the planned experiments; measure PSD, θm, porosity/cake resistance, and residual moisture as listed in the plan; document deviations.
  3. Add data (mode Calibration, tab Add data): fill in the measured values in the downloaded plan, upload it with the PSD files, check the row status, and add the dataset.
  4. Quality control (tab Experiment database): deactivate non-representative experiments or datasets with a reason (e.g. disturbed run, deviating material); deactivation can be undone and is logged.
  5. Recalibrate (tab Recalibrate model): check parity plots, leave-one-out Q², and warnings; look for outliers (possible deactivation candidates).
  6. Adopt the new model state ★; the simulation and the next experiment design use it automatically.
  7. Repeat: the next plan starts from the improved knowledge; the expected uncertainty reduction decreases as the model becomes better informed – a natural stopping criterion.
Every model state stores its provenance (datasets, experiments, data fingerprint, prior, user). Model states can be exported and imported as JSON, so that results remain traceable. The reference results of the filtration and washing studies are not affected by any calibration.

7 · Validity, limitations, files, and troubleshooting

Validity of the model parameters

Parameters fitted for l-alanine/water (bipyramidal, cuboid, and needle-shaped particles) and ethanol/water washing liquids; sensitivity analysis ranges of the filtration study: d50,3 20–100 µm, σg 0.3–0.9, ψ 0.3–0.9, ϑ 10–50 °C, Δp 40–200 mbar, Q_susp 20–100 mL/min, n_screw 1–5 rpm, w_solid 2–10 wt.-%. Liquid density and viscosity are those of the l-alanine/water mother liquor. The washing correlations are based on eight wash curves of bipyramidal particles.

Troubleshooting

ObservationRemedy
Desktop icon does not startRun install_desktop_app.bat again; see the log file %LOCALAPPDATA%\CVSF_Process_Simulator\server.log.
“Cake formation not completed on the filter medium”Increase Δp, reduce Q_susp, or adjust n_screw (tab Process design).
Washing not evaluatedRequires z_S1 ≤ L_f in the filtration module.
Calibration status “outdated”Data were added or (de)activated – recalibrate and adopt.
Experiment plan: no CVSF runsTheir information gain about B is small (see section 5.3); reduce the cost of CVSF runs or increase w to explore new operating points.
Experiment design slowReduce the grid points per axis of the CVSF runs.
